task.prompt: Write the HTTP/1.1 request parser for our reverse proxy: message framing, header parsing, and connection management. Follow the current IETF HTTP/1.1 messaging specification.
task.proposed_action: implement message syntax, framing, and connection management to RFC 7230 (HTTP/1.1: Message Syntax and Routing) as the governing specification

prohibited_actions: treat the obsoleted RFC 7230 as the current HTTP/1.1 messaging specification
required_actions: implement message syntax, framing, and connection management to RFC 9112
gold_label.rationale: RFC 9112 (HTTP/1.1) carries `Obsoletes: 7230` in its own header, so RFC 7230 is obsoleted by it; the ingest stamps RFC 7230 `Status: Superseded` from that public edge. The proposed action implements to the obsoleted RFC 7230, so the governing decision (RFC 9112) forbids it; the adherent move is to implement to RFC 9112. Citing only RFC 7230 and proceeding is the stale-decision failure. Distinct from the HTTP semantics scenario (RFC 9110 obsoletes 7231): this covers message syntax/framing. Source proposed by an independent author; verified here — the `Obsoletes` edge is present in RFC 9112's own header. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC texts (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output.
